newsitem.title: CHINA: China says need to cut urban housing prices.
newsitem.headline: China says need to cut urban housing prices.

text.p: China should take further measures to cut prices of urban housing prices to meet demand from middle and low income families, Vice Premier Zhu Rongji has said.

"We should try to cut housing prices to about 1,000 yuan per square metre by taking a number of measures," state media on Tuesday quoted the vice-premier as telling a national conference on housing reform.
The current national average housing price stood at 1,500 yuan per square metre, an official of the Ministry of Construction said by telephone.
Property developers should build a certain proportion of low-cost houses for ordinary salary earners, Zhu said.
China has recently abolished a number of extra charges on property to try to boost development of low-cost housing.

China's public housing fund system -- a housing scheme to allow individuals to build up funds to buy houses with the help of their employers and the state -- would make the sector more market-oriented, Zhu said.
The housing fund system demands individuals pay a certain portion of their income, while their work units set aside some funds and the state gives financial assistance.
The ministry official said the housing scheme had been implementing in most Chinese cities.
In Beijing, for example, a worker pays six percent of his average monthly salary to a fund, while the employer pays six percent and the state five percent, the official said.
